t: This is the Hunterian Museum, a collection of anatomical specimens housed in the building of the Royal College of Surgeons of England. It takes its name from John Hunter, the Scottish surgeon, who was one of the most distinguished scientists and surgeons of his day. He argued for careful observation and scientific method in medicine, and he taught and worked with Edward Jenner, who pioneered the smallpox vaccine. So the museum is a fitting place to think about how medicine became a science.
